newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded prices ease in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded prices ease in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices fell in Chicago on Thursday, driven lower by easing differentials as sellers finally emerged after nearly a week on the sidelines, traders said.
Talk of firmness in Chicago stocks was offset by news Clark Refining and Marketing Co restarted a fluid catalytic cracker at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery, traders said.
An Illinois court last week cleared the way for the unit to restart, and Clark had said gasoline output would double to about two million gallons a day from the Chicago-area refinery.
"That's our normal capacity and we should be just about there," a Clark spokeswoman said. An alkylation unit idled after the October 19 fire has not been restarted, she said.

Gasoline stocks on hand at Midwest refineries remained 1.5 million barrels below the same week last year, while distillate stocks were 1.39 million barrels below last year's levels, the American Petroleum Institute reported Wednesday.

Chicago prompt unleaded gasoline eased to 6.0/6.25 cents a gallon over NYMEX December unleaded, a nearly two cent a gallon drop on the day. Later deliveries were talked 3.50/3.75 cents a gallon over the print.
Group Three unleaded basis also eroded, easing to bids 5.0 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 2.0 cents over for later deliveries, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel eased to 3.25/3.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX December heating oil for prompt deliveries and 2.25/2.50 cents over the print for later deliveries.
Group Three prompt low sulphur was talked 3.0/3.25 cents a gallon over the print, with later deliveries 1.50/1.75 cents over, traders said.
